messages:
deploy-bot: init rollout for feature flag 'header-normalization' on service `request-gateway` in ap-southeast-1. plan: 1% -> 8% -> 30% with 15m soak windows. runtime pinned to v2.4.1 for canaries. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/header-normalization

emily: starting 1% canary now. quiet window 01:00-05:00 local. watching p50/p95, 5xx, and cache miss rate.

raj: monitoring checklist live: p50/p95, 4xx/5xx, cache miss, token cost delta, downstream latency. paging thresholds set at 0.5% 5xx.

tony: executing:```
ffops set --flag header-normalization --env prod --pct 1 --by "emily"
```

ops-bot: infra snapshot OK, no pod restarts. grafana link: https://obs.internal/d/header-norm

emily: 1% routed. p95 +200ms compared to baseline, p50 unchanged. 5xx 0.06% (baseline 0.02%). small drift but < emergency threshold.

raj: noticing cache misses up ~3% correlated to header key change. investigating quick toggle to preserve legacy header mapping.

deploy-bot: auto-advance scheduled to 8% at +12m if gates pass.

emily: i'm going to pause auto-advance to validate downstream cache behavior for 20m. holding.

tony: auto-advance paused by emily. to continue run: `/ffops approve header-normalization --next 8` or rollback: `/ffops rollback header-normalization`.

ops-bot: metrics t+8m: p95 steady, cache miss still elevated but steady. 5xx at 0.08%. no OOMs.

emily: decision: hold until raj's header-mapping hotfix merged. tagging release notes: "pause at 1% due to cache miss increase; hotfix required to keep legacy header keys."

raj: opened PR #4821 with a normalization toggle and compatibility layer. aim to merge in ~10m.

support-bot: notified pinned enterprise customers that their traffic is excluded from this canary. message template used.

emily: agree no rollback. manual resume after hotfix and 10m soak post-merge. will update thread when ready. :eyes:
